figures.caption: Figure 1: The in-house model as released. Each channel passes through the sinc front-end (Eq. 1), which acts as a low-pass filter below one hertz as implemented, and a patch convolution; tokens add electrode-position and temporal embeddings (Eq. 2). The encoder reads the unmasked window, masking replaces its outputs by a mask token before the predictor, and the projected prediction is regressed onto the stop-gradient projection of the encoder output, with SIGReg on that projection (Eqs. 3 and 4). Only the encoder is evaluated downstream.

Table 1: Original benchmarks: task, classes, windows per split (five seconds at 200 Hz, read from the evaluation outputs) and the split rule. TUSL and TUAB draw a new subject-disjoint split for every seed (sizes shown for the first seed); the other three keep one split. The TUSL positive class is rare, so AUROC is reported.

Figure 2: Layer-wise probe protocol. (a) A linear probe at every internal stage of the frozen encoder (twelve for the in-house model), with the band power anchor on the same split. (b) Per-stage mechanics: mean-pool over tokens, standardise on the training split, logistic regression. (c) The gap G is the peak minus the output stage, with the peak ŝ selected on validation (Eq. 5; measured curves in Figure 3).

Figure 3: Layer-wise frozen probe (test AUROC) for three cells of the leakage-free benchmarks (all cells in Appendix D). Solid: pretrained; dashed: random-init; dotted: band power; circle: test-argmax stage; star: validation-selected stage. Left: a genuine early-stage peak that the random twin reproduces. Middle: validation picks an early stage while the test argmax sits one stage before the output. Right: the largest selection penalty.

Figure 4: Added task families, frozen probe at the validation-selected stage (mean ± std over 3 seeds; a deterministic probe has no bar): pretrained (circles), random-init (squares) and each model’s matched band power (grey bar). LuMamba was not run under the within-subject MI protocol. Numbers in Appendix E.

Table 3: Gain ∆ of full fine-tuning, pretrained minus random-init at the best-validation epoch (test metric), mean±population std over 5 seeds, on the five original benchmarks; bold = mean beyond twice its seed std. k = datasets with a positive mean. The in-house Lee2019 cells carry developer contact with that benchmark (Section 5.3).

Figure 5: Full fine-tuning gain ∆ per model and benchmark. Filled markers: mean beyond twice the seed standard deviation. The in-house Lee2019 cell carries developer contact with that benchmark (Section 5.3).
Table 6: Protocol constants, read from the evaluation code at build time.

Table 7: What the released in-house front-end passes. Top: share of spectral power per band (%) in Lee2019 (first 32 windows, all channels), at the input, at the output of the released front-end, and at the output of the same filters with the time index in samples (n instead of n/fs in Eq. 1; not retrained). Bottom: gain (output over input amplitude) for pure sines, for four of the filters.

Figure 6: Layer-wise frozen linear probe for every pretrained cell of the three leakage-free benchmarks (rows: datasets; columns: models; x-axis: probed stage from input to output). Solid: pretrained; dashed: random-init; dotted: band power; circle: test-argmax stage; star: validation-selected stage.

Table 8: Frozen probe on the three leakage-free original benchmarks, both initialisations (36 cells): validationselected peak minus output stage (selection penalty = test-argmax minus validation-selected peak, in parentheses). APAVA and Lee2019 report AUROC, BCI IV 2a accuracy; the in-house Lee2019 cells carry developer contact with that benchmark.

Table 9: Frozen linear probe on the four added task families: validation-selected stage, test metric, mean of 3 seeds; ∆ = pretrained − random-init, computed before rounding; last row = five-band log-power baseline on the same split. Seed std ≤ 0.024; on the within-subject protocols the split is deterministic, so pretrained is a point estimate and only random-init carries a seed band. The band-power baseline is computed on each model’s own preprocessed input; each model is compared with its own baseline (seed mean, std ≤ 0.023), and the last row gives the range over models. MI within-subject: 5 models, as LuMamba was not run under that protocol.

Table 11: Trainable attention-pooling readout on frozen features (3 seeds) against the mean-pool linear probe at the output stage. d = attention minus mean-pool; a non-positive d means the native-style readout does not recover the output layer.

Table 13: Tuned anchor for full fine-tuning (one seed): each model’s learning rate chosen from 2e-5, 5e-5, 1e-4 by minimum validation loss, against the canonical rate of the main matrix. The penalty is what the canonical protocol gives away; a positive value means tuning would have helped.

Table 15: Pretrained minus random-init validation-selected peak as the labelled training fraction shrinks, mean±std over 3 seeds, from a separate feature-extraction run (one initialisation per cell). The original benchmarks use fixed splits and the linear probe is deterministic, so at the full budget the seed acts on nothing and the std is zero; seeds act only through the subsampling below it. A low-label advantage would show as a gap that grows to the left.

Table 18: Frozen linear probe on the five original benchmarks as released (test-argmax peak stage, five seeds): pretrained / random-init peak; last row the five-band log-power baseline. Within-subject and fixed splits give a zero seed std for the pretrained probe. Validation-selected values for the three leakage-free benchmarks are in Table 8; the in-house Lee2019 cells carry developer contact with that benchmark.

Table 19: Development-record values of the in-house model (Section 4.1). No raw output survives for these; each value is copied from the project document line shown, and the build fails when the value is no longer on that line.
